chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Marwan ibn Ubayd, from Jumay' ibn Amr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is (Allah is the Greatest)?'

I replied: 'Allah is greater than everything.' He said: 'And there was a thing, so would it be greater than Him?' I said: 'Then what is its meaning?' He replied: 'Allah is greater than what can be attributed to Him with any meaning (of the First and the Last).'
ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of 'Allahu Akbar' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs a dialectical argument to refute the notion that 'Allahu Akbar' implies a comparative magnitude relative to creation, noting that such a comparison would be invalid prior to the existence of created things. This establishes the phrase as a declaration of Allah's absolute transcendence (tanzih), signifying that He is greater than any attribute or description that can be ascribed to Him. This insight underscores the Shia theological emphasis on divine incomparability, distinguishing Allah's essence from all contingent beings.
